BiblicalUsage: Nakeh means smitten or maimed, and in its tenderest use it means poor and contrite in spirit. In 2 Samuel 4:4 Jonathan's son is lame of his feet, five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan, and his nurse took him up and fled, and he fell and became lame, and in Isaiah 66:2 the Lord says He will look to the one who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembles at His word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lame child and the contrite heart belong together in this word, because both are smitten and both are seen by God; mephibosheth fell and was lame for life, and the Lord looks to the one who trembles at His word.
